BABA and BAA policies: Two key policies govern domestic content requirements for both federal acquisition and the use of federal funds in infrastructure projects: the Buy American Act (BAA) and the Build America, Buy America Act (BABA). These laws aim to increase the domestic content of goods procured under federal agency projects and/or infrastructure projects using federal funds. BAA pertains to contracts with federal agencies while BABA applies to federally funded infrastructure projects requiring iron, steel, manufactured products, and construction materials (Putsche et al. 2024). Although these policies aim to support American manufacturing, they present challenges for hydropower developers, asset owners, and equipment manufacturers because American manufacturers and suppliers are limited in the current market. Developers, owners, operators, and suppliers in hydropower face challenges finding equipment that meets standards, especially for large hydropower projects. While projects may seek waivers if a product is unavailable (in sufficient quantity or quality), increases the project cost by over 25%, or is inconsistent with the public interest, attaining these waivers can often take time and resources and may not be possible in certain circumstances. At the time of writing, the Made in America waiver library contains 2,293 proposed or approved waivers (Made in America n.d.). A submitted waiver may be challenged or protested by the funding agency. Manufacturers must monitor their waiver’s status in this portal and await the Office of Management and Budget determination. Because most major hydropower components, including LPTs, are fabricated to custom specifications and are site-specific, adhering to compliance and documentation rules sometimes makes the procurement process harder. While the BAA can provide long-term benefits for the hydropower sector and enhance the industry’s self-sufficiency in supply chain capacity, it poses industry concern about near-term supply chain bottlenecks and the reliability of the grid as domestic production capacity struggles to meet ongoing demand. 18 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies at www.nlr.gov/publications. 2 Domestic Content Eligibility Federal policies continue to evolve to support the domestic manufacture of steel and iron. The Inflation Reduction Act established, and the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA) modified, a domestic content bonus credit under the investment tax credit and production tax credit, which provides an additional 10 percentage points of credit value for projects that meet domestic content requirements. In May 2024, Internal Revenue Service (IRS) Notice 2024-41 provided a safe harbor table for hydropower and pumped storage hydropower (PSH) projects to help them more easily qualify for the bonus credit.
